Nextflow workflow

2026-08-18

Runs processed: 260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX (LK1 re-sequenced), 260528_VH01624_464_222K7VKNX (LK2) and 260717_VH01624_477_222KG22NX (LK3).

Analysis finished: 2026-08-18 - the most recent of the 6 figures shown below.

Report generated: 2026-08-18 by 03.nextflow_workflow_report.Rmd, from the outputs of steps 01-02 in this folder.

Everything the benchmark reports settled - cell calling, demultiplexing, ADT normalisation, annotation, CNV calling - is implemented once, as a Nextflow pipeline, and run over every sequencing run from raw FASTQ to a final annotated object. This report describes what the pipeline is, what it produced, and where its settings agree or disagree with the benchmarks that were supposed to determine them.

For full report, download nextflow_workflow_report.html in the attachment and open in a browser.

The pipeline lives in a different repository from the lab archives: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome

Code used for this report - attached and in: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome_dev/tree/main/lab_archives/9.Nextflow_workflow

Aim

Document the production pipeline as it actually stands, and check it against the benchmarks:

  • what does the workflow do, in what order, with what resources
  • does every process actually run
  • do the parameters match what the benchmark reports concluded
  • what did it produce for each run, and where do cells get lost

Conclusions

  • the pipeline runs end to end on all three runs. Every one of the 13 published stages is present for LK1 re-sequenced, LK2 and LK3, through to a final merged object and a per-run QC report
  • most settings match their benchmarks - emptyDrops FDR 0.01 and minimum 100 UMI, HTO positive.quantile 0.99, cellSNP min count 20 and MAF 0.10, genotype demultiplexing with cellSNP-lite plus vireo, DSB for ADT, CellBender 0.3.0, refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A
  • the annotation threshold does not match. bin/annotate.R runs BoneMarrowMap at MAD_threshold = 4; bin/lib_early_qc_annotation.R and every standalone script use the default 2.5. Report 07 shows this roughly halves the rejection rate, so results_nf/ and results/seurat_annotated/ are not directly comparable
  • params.cell_caller is a dead parameter that says the wrong thing. It is set to "emptydrops" and is never read anywhere. The workflow assigns CellBender barcodes as the primary cell calls unconditionally. Anyone changing that parameter expecting an effect would get none
  • DOROTHEA_VIPER never runs. The module and its R script exist, but the process is the only one of the 20 that is neither included nor called in main.nf
  • demultiplexing is where the cells go. It is the largest single loss in every run - LK2 drops from 33,228 scDblFinder singlets to 25,690 demultiplexed cells, about 23%. Cell calling and mapping QC are minor by comparison
  • the two cell callers disagree more than expected, and not evenly. Jaccard overlap is 91.9% for LK1 but only 74.5% for LK2, and CellBender always calls more barcodes - 8,895 CellBender-only against 1,349 emptyDrops-only in LK2. Since CellBender is the primary caller and emptyDrops feeds the DSB background, the two are both in use and their disagreement propagates
  • the pipeline runs the re-sequenced LK1, not the pilot. 260522 is in the samplesheet; 260423 is not. Reports 01, 07 and 08 analysed the pilot. The two trees look interchangeable and are not
  • donor names differ between the pipeline and the standalone work - HBDN206-MN-pCT against HBDN206-MNpCT, HBDN392-MDS against HBDN392-AML-MDS, HBDN501-KMT2A against HBDN501-AML-KMT2A. Joins between the two output trees will not match on donor

1. What the pipeline is

A single main.nf with 18 modules, run on SLURM through run_nextflow.sh, publishing to results_nf/<run>/. Each process is a thin Nextflow wrapper around an R script in bin/, so the analysis code is readable on its own and the .nf file carries only the plumbing.

conf/samples.csv - the only thing that has to change to add a run
run sample_short sample_name n_donors donor_ids unhashed
260528_VH01624_464_222K7VKNX LK2 LK2-GEX 4 HBDN498-TP53;APOP576-TP53;HBDN376-TP53;normal-01 NA
260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX LK1 LK1-GEX 4 MOLM13;HBDN206-MN-pCT;HBDN392-MDS;HBDN501-KMT2A NA
260717_VH01624_477_222KG22NX LK3 LK3-GEX 3 normal_CD34-01;;;normal-02 WEI21_26-17_NK

The samplesheet carries the run, the sample, the donor count and the semicolon-joined donor IDs. LK3’s donor_ids field - normal_CD34-01;;;normal-02 - shows two conventions at once: the empty slots are HTO positions that were not used, and WEI21_26-17_NK is an unhashed donor carried in its own column, assigned downstream by whichever vireo genetic cluster does not match an HTO singlet population.

DOROTHEA_VIPER is declared in modules/dorothea_viper.nf with a matching bin/dorothea_viper.R, and is neither included nor invoked. It is dead code rather than a disabled option - there is no parameter that would switch it on.

3. Parameters against the benchmarks

This is the part that matters. Each benchmark report exists to settle one setting; the pipeline is where those decisions are supposed to end up.

Pipeline setting against the benchmark that determined it
setting pipeline_value benchmark_conclusion report verdict
emptyDrops FDR 0.01 FDR <= 0.01 04 cell calling matches
emptyDrops minimum UMI 100 100 04 cell calling matches
primary cell caller CellBender (hardcoded in main.nf) CellBender for cell calls, emptyDrops retained for DSB background 04 cell calling matches the DAG, contradicts params.cell_caller
params.cell_caller "emptydrops" n/a - the parameter is never read 04 cell calling dead parameter
HTO positive.quantile 0.99 0.99 03 demultiplexing matches
demultiplexing method cellSNP-lite + vireo, compared against HTO genotyping outperforms HTO hashing 03 demultiplexing matches
cellSNP min count 20 20 03 demultiplexing matches
cellSNP min MAF 0.10 0.10 03 demultiplexing matches
ADT normalisation DSB, in CITE_QC DSB outperforms CLR 05 CITE-seq matches
BoneMarrowMap MAD_threshold 4 (bin/annotate.R) 2.5 - the default, and what the standalone scripts used 07 cell type annotation differs
Numbat container "${params.proj_dir}/containers/numbat-rbase_latest.sif" version not recorded - latest tag 08 calling cancer cells unpinned
CellBender container "${params.proj_dir}/containers/cellbender_0.3.0_fixed.sif" CellBender 0.3.0 04 cell calling matches
transcriptome "${params.annotation_dir}/refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A" refdata-gex-GRCh38-2024-A 01 LK1 pilot matches

Two rows need attention.

MAD_threshold. bin/annotate.R - the script the live ANNOTATE process runs - uses 4. bin/lib_early_qc_annotation.R uses 2.5, and so did every standalone annotation script. Report 07 measured what this costs: rejection drops from 7.95% to 3.91% in the pilot and from 5.48% to 1.75% in LK2. The cells recovered are shallow, ribosome-poor and enriched for HTO negatives, which argues for 2.5. Whichever is preferred, the two code paths should agree with each other, and right now they do not.

params.cell_caller. Declared as "emptydrops" in nextflow.config and never read. The workflow does cell_barcodes = CELLBENDER.out.cellbender_barcodes with no conditional. The behaviour is right - report 04 concluded CellBender for cell calls with emptyDrops retained for the DSB background, which is exactly what the DAG does - but the parameter documents the opposite and would mislead anyone reading the config to find out what the pipeline does.

Demultiplexing is consistently the largest loss. In LK2 it removes 7,538 cells, against 348 lost to mapping QC at the other end. That is the expected shape - pooled donors mean every ambiguous or doublet droplet is discarded - but it is worth knowing that the dominant attrition in the pipeline is the pooling design, not any QC threshold.

02_cell_caller_overlap.pdf

Both callers run on every sample, and both outputs are used - CellBender’s barcodes are the cell calls, emptyDrops’ barcodes define the background droplets DSB needs. So the overlap is not academic: the two sets disagree by 25% in LK2, and each disagreement region feeds a different part of the downstream analysis.

7. Runtime

Nextflow writes no trace file here - only report and dag are enabled in the config - but its HTML execution report embeds the full per-task trace as JSON, which is where these numbers come from. They are Nextflow’s own accounting, not a re-measurement.

Per run. wall_total_if_serial is the sum of task runtimes, not elapsed time
run n_tasks cached failed wall_total_if_serial cpu_hours
260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX 28 0 0 24:52:50 268.35
260528_VH01624_464_222K7VKNX 28 27 0 35:02:14 351.04
260717_VH01624_477_222KG22NX 25 25 0 28:07:50 284.82
Elapsed wall clock against work done. concurrency = work / elapsed
run elapsed_h work_h concurrency
260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX 11.58 24.88 2.15
260528_VH01624_464_222K7VKNX 23.59 35.04 1.48
260717_VH01624_477_222KG22NX 16.55 28.13 1.70

CACHED is a success, not a failure - it means Nextflow resumed that task from a previous run’s work directory instead of re-executing it. LK1 was executed in full; LK2 and LK3 are almost entirely resumed. No task failed in any run.

06_pipeline_timeline.pdf

One bar per task, positioned from the first submit of its run. Overlapping bars ran concurrently, so panel width is elapsed time while the total bar length is work done. The long serial spine at the start - Cell Ranger, then CellBender and cellSNP - is what sets the floor on how fast a run can finish.

03_runtime_by_process.pdf

04_cpu_hours_by_process.pdf

Allocated CPU hours - realtime times allocated cpus, so what the process costs the cluster rather than what it uses.

05_peak_memory_by_process.pdf

Peak RSS per task against the memory each process asks for. CITE_SEQ_COUNT_ADT is the one to look at.

Three things stand out. CopyKAT is the most expensive step - 10h19m of wall clock across its four per-donor tasks in LK2, more than Cell Ranger. The pipeline is only 1.5-2.2x concurrent, because the early stages are a serial chain on one sample before the per-donor fan-out begins. And CITE_SEQ_COUNT_ADT peaks at 311 GB RSS, which is worth checking against what its process directive actually requests.

9. Observations

Recorded rather than fixed - the pipeline is a separate repository and nothing in this report modifies it.

Things worth deciding about
issue where detail
params.cell_caller is declared and never used nextflow.config It is set to “emptydrops”, but the workflow assigns cell_barcodes = CELLBENDER.out.cellbender_barcodes unconditionally. The parameter says the opposite of what the DAG does, and changing it would have no effect.
MAD_threshold differs between the two annotation code paths bin/annotate.R vs bin/lib_early_qc_annotation.R annotate.R, the live ANNOTATE process, uses 4. lib_early_qc_annotation.R uses the BoneMarrowMap default of 2.5. The standalone benchmark scripts also used 2.5, so results_nf and results/seurat_annotated are not directly comparable.
leftover debug logging in the workflow main.nf A log.info marked “TEMP DEBUG - remove once NUMBAT_PILEUP null-path bug is confirmed fixed” still fires for every donor of every run.
donor names differ between the pipeline and the standalone analyses conf/samples.csv samples.csv has HBDN206-MN-pCT, HBDN392-MDS, HBDN501-KMT2A; the standalone scripts and results use HBDN206-MNpCT, HBDN392-AML-MDS, HBDN501-AML-KMT2A. Same donors, different strings, so joins between the two output trees will not match on donor.
the Numbat container is pinned to latest nextflow.config numbat_sif points at numbat-rbase_latest.sif. The version that produced the published results is not recoverable from the image name.
conda environments are absolute paths in one home directory nextflow.config r_env, cite_seq_count_env, cellsnp_env and cellranger_bin are all under /home/nbartonicek, so the pipeline only runs as this user.
DOROTHEA_VIPER is a dead module modules/dorothea_viper.nf, bin/dorothea_viper.R The module and its R script exist, but the process is neither included nor called anywhere in main.nf, so it never runs. It is the only module of the 18 that is not wired into the workflow.

10. What was run

Step Script What
01 01.pipeline_inventory.R Parses modules/, main.nf and nextflow.config into process, parameter and resource tables, and checks which processes are actually wired into the workflow.
02a 02a.pipeline_runtimes.R Parses the per-task trace out of Nextflow’s HTML execution reports and summarises runtime, CPU hours, peak memory and the schedule.
02 02.pipeline_outputs_and_params.R Inventories the published output tree per run, reads the cell-count funnel and cell-caller overlap, and compares every parameter against the benchmark that determined it.
03 03.nextflow_workflow_report.Rmd This report.

Unlike reports 01-08 there are no analysis scripts of mine to collate here - the pipeline itself is the artefact. These two steps read it and write down what they find; neither writes anything into nextflow/.

12. Caveats

  • this report describes the pipeline as it stands on the reporting branch of the surface_proteome repository at the time of writing. It is a live repository and can move underneath this description
  • the parameter-versus-benchmark table is a judgement about intent, not a measurement. It records what each benchmark report concluded and what the pipeline does; where they agree, that agreement was not re-verified by re-running anything
  • the cell-count funnel and cell-caller overlap tables are the pipeline’s own QC output, read as published. They were not recomputed from the objects
  • results_nf/ and results/seurat_annotated/ are different analyses of overlapping data, at different annotation thresholds, on partly different runs, with different donor naming. Numbers should not be carried between them without checking all three
  • runtime numbers come from Nextflow’s execution reports. For a CACHED task the timestamps are those of the run that actually executed it, not of the resumed invocation, so the timelines for LK2 and LK3 show the original schedule
  • CPU hours are allocated, not consumed - a process given 16 cores that uses one still bills 16
  • nothing in this report modifies the pipeline. The observations in section 8 are for you to decide about
